title: Dull — by sameness, by length, by pace
core: All five are verdicts of dullness, and all five blame the same culprit: nothing worth attending to is happening. They split on *why* your attention died. Two of them indict sameness — the thing never varies. Two indict duration — the thing will not stop. One indicts pace — the thing moves, but heavily. Getting the right one means asking which of those three the sentence actually gives you evidence for.

words.nuance: **Monotonous** attacks *variation* — one note, one texture, held. It's the only one at home describing raw sensory sameness in a short stretch: a droning voice for five minutes is monotonous, never humdrum. The verdict is numbness, attention sliding off.

**Humdrum** is the long-horizon one — it measures in years, not minutes, and attaches to whole lives, towns, jobs, marriages. Uniquely, the thing itself may be perfectly nice; the grumble is only that it repeats. Tonally it sighs at one's own existence rather than insulting someone else's.

**Tedious** is the patience word: the thing stopped being interesting and then kept going. It implies *easy* — hard work can grip you, tedious work is trivial and endless. It's the polite, printable complaint, the one you can put in a report about a document without sounding rude.

**Interminable** claims only endlessness — it makes no charge of sameness at all. It's hyperbole about the sufferer, not the clock, and it needs a captive: meetings, sermons, queues, delays you must sit through. The most exasperated word here.

**Plodding** is the only one about *pace and weight* — trudging, no lightness, no spark. It's also the only one that can carry grudging respect, since the plodder is often thorough and does finish. Aimed at a mind rather than a walk, it means unimaginative: incapable of a leap.

exam_note: The exam plants the deciding clue outside the blank — "day after day, identical" wants monotonous/humdrum, "three hours in, still talking" wants tedious/interminable, "slow and heavy but reliable" wants plodding; only plodding survives a positive clause.
